# Game model (16px logical grid, 32x32 cells; cell (col,row) = x/16, y/16)

## Layout
- Left = workspace (cols 0-15, rows 5-26). Col 16 = dashed divider. Right = black panel with
  colored "mold" shapes (trapezoids) = CLICKABLE BUTTONS, one per color.
- Bottom strip = budget/timer bar: shrinks ~4px per action (512px total => ~128 actions).
  A bad/rolled-back move cost ~80px (20 actions). Avoid invalid moves.

## Entities
- Colored 1-cell dot inside a 3x3 gray pad: GREEN dot = player (moves 1 cell per ACTION1..4:
  up/down/left/right). It walks on any solid tile (gray, blue, red...). It cannot enter empty
  space or checkered (ghost) cells. It is a free walker, not bound to its pad.
- YELLOW dot in another 3x3 gray pad = goal (hypothesis).
- Checkered (半-cell checkerboard) 2x2 area = GHOST slot: the alternate position of a block.
- Solid colored blocks = bridges/ladders/platforms.

## Actions
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move green dot up/down/left/right one cell (no-op if blocked; no-op costs budget).
- ACTION6 on a mold button (right panel) = TOGGLE that color's block between its two
  configurations (position and/or orientation both can change; e.g. red 3x2 horizontal <->
  2x3 vertical elsewhere). Blue's alternate slot is drawn as the checkered ghost.
- ACTION6 elsewhere (workspace, pads, dots) = no effect.
- DANGER: toggling the block the dot is standing on strands the dot -> iris animation rollback
  with heavy budget penalty.
- ACTION5/ACTION7/RESET not available.

## Strategy
Read the board as a graph: use toggles to build a path from the green dot to the goal, ordering
toggles so the dot is always on a static tile when a toggle fires.

# Game model (ARC-style puzzle: walk a dot to the goal)

## Grid & display
- 16px logical cells; standard 512x512 view => 32x32 cells. Left = workspace, a dashed column
  (white 16px dashes on alternating rows) separates it from the right BLACK PANEL of buttons.
- Bottom strip = per-level budget/timer bar (white = remaining). Consumption per action varies by
  level (level 1-4: ~4px/action => ~128 actions; level 5: ~1.5px/action => ~330 actions).
- Colors come in light/dark pairs per "family" (e.g. #F93C31/#921231 red, #FF7BCC/#E53AA3 pink,
  #1E93FF blue, #CCCCCC/#999999 gray, #FF851B orange = "track segment completely filled").

## Objects
- GREEN 1-cell dot = player; ACTION1..4 = up/down/left/right, one cell per action, no diagonals.
  It walks on any solid tile (gray/red/blue/purple/pink/orange/white floor). Cannot enter empty
  space or checkered ghost cells. No-op moves still cost budget.
- YELLOW 1-cell dot = goal. Stepping on it completes the level.
- Checkered (8px checkerboard) region = GHOST: the alternate position/shape of a movable block.
- Small "hill/trapezoid" GLYPH drawn centered on a 2x2 gray pad = locked button token: walk onto
  that pad to add that color's button to the right panel.
- Pink/magenta checkered single cell = TELEPORT slot; there are exactly two per level. Standing on
  one and clicking the magenta button teleports the player to the other.
- Levers: light-colored arms + dark 2x2 pivot; the color button rotates the arms 90 degrees about
  the pivot (arms end up in the pivot's columns/rows). Gray 2x2 end caps are static.
- Multi-part toggles: one click can move/materialize several blocks at once (e.g. 1 block <-> 3
  blocks; or make two ghost regions solid simultaneously). Blocks may change shape between states.
- CHAINS (level 4/5): "yellow L" and "gray square" buttons step chains one cell along fixed loops.
  Tracks are drawn black when empty (sometimes invisible), light gray when occupied, orange when a
  chain exactly fills a segment. A chain can be "walked with": click, then step onto the newly
  covered cell (the player must remain covered after each click).
- Level 5 introduced a red "snake" on a white floor region moved by four small cyan/blue buttons
  (left/up/right/down, 2 cells per step). When it wraps around a tab on a big orange bar it becomes
  coupled and horizontal moves push/pull that bar; the red-bar button then reshapes the snake.

## Rules
- ACTION6 works ONLY on right-panel buttons; workspace clicks are inert.
- Never toggle the block the player is standing on: the player is not carried; the game rolls the
  move back with a large budget penalty (~20 actions' worth).
- Plan order so the player always stands on static ground when a toggle fires.
- ACTION5/ACTION7/RESET are not offered.

## Method that works
1. Map the board at 16px (sample at x=16k+4 to avoid 8px grid lines); re-read at 8px to find
   checkered ghosts, glyphs and offset objects.
2. Build a connectivity graph of solid regions; find which toggles add the missing edges.
3. Execute, re-checking the player's cell after each move (read_pixels is free).

# Board model
- 16px logical cells => 32x32 grid in the 512x512 view. Left = workspace (#333333 bg),
  right = BLACK panel of buttons; a dashed white column (col 20, white on even rows) is only
  decoration — floor (e.g. a goal platform) can extend under/past it.
- Bottom strip = budget bar (white = remaining). ~0.75px/action; a rolled-back illegal action
  costs ~10x.

## Walkable vs not (level 6 semantics)
- Walkable: gray pads (#999999), the orange lever/key, light-gray chain (#CCCCCC) + its orange
  "full segment" cells, red snake cells.
- NOT walkable: WHITE regions (they are the *machinery track* for snake/lever pivots), dark bg.

# Objects
- GREEN 1-cell dot = player (ACTION1..4 = up/down/left/right, 1 cell, no diagonals).
- YELLOW 1-cell cell = goal; stepping on it wins the level.
- ORANGE LEVER ("key"): long 10x2 arm + 2 short side nubs + a 2x2 red-outlined PIVOT.
  Rotates 90° about its pivot when its colour button is pressed. Rotating while the player
  stands on a cell that would become empty => rollback + big budget penalty (standing on the
  pivot is always safe).
- RED SNAKE: drawn as a hollow ring (8px-thick outline). Moved 2 CELLS per press by the 4 arms
  of the panel "cross". May pass over dark space; its centre must stay on the white track.
- Coupling (crucial): drive the snake so its hole surrounds the lever's PIVOT, then press the
  RED BAR button => the snake contracts onto the pivot. From then on the cross buttons drag the
  LEVER with the snake (pivot must follow the white track: use corridors/rooms as a maze).
- CHAIN: light-gray body on a hidden loop track; the colour button (yellow L) steps it one
  position (period 6 here). Stepping is rolled back (penalty) if the player's own cell would
  become uncovered — stand on a cell covered by all configurations you step through.
- TELEPORT NODES: 2-colour checkerboard cells (light+dark of one family: yellow/orange,
  red/darkred, cyan/blue, pink/magenta). One node is VARIABLE; a 4-colour panel button cycles
  its colour (red->yellow->cyan->pink->...). The MAGENTA trapezoid = universal teleport between
  the variable node and the node whose colour matches; it ALSO rotates the lever every press
  (so two teleports restore the lever's orientation — use this to keep a bridge intact).
- Hub islands with a 3x3 pad: 4 checkered pads (colour dot each) around a node. Standing on a
  pad ENABLES that colour's cross button (its panel arm lights up); the button is dead otherwise.
- Hill/trapezoid glyph on a pad = locked-button token: walk onto it to add that button.

# Hard-won practical rules
1. ACTION6 must hit the button's actual painted shape. Measure the icon's pixel extent and click
   its CENTRE. Clicking a few pixels outside (e.g. on the coloured dot's corner) silently does
   nothing — this cost me ~100 wasted actions.
2. Frame counts read like a status code: 1 frame = applied or ignored; 3 frames = move blocked;
   6 frames = button refused (its target object pulses — great for identifying what a button
   controls); 15 frames (iris wipe) = illegal action rolled back with a budget penalty.
3. Free tools (read_pixels/inspect) are the main instrument: scan 64x64 (8px) for object
   geometry, and diff scans across turns to see what a button changed.
4. Long bars are usually the exact width of a gap: measure gaps in cells and look for an object
   of that length — it's the intended bridge.

[After action · message]
**Game complete — WIN, 6/6 levels.**

## How the final level was solved

The last level hinged on three discoveries:

1. **A click-targeting bug in my own model.** The panel's "cross" of four coloured arms had my old coordinates recorded at the *dots'* corners, which landed on black background — so every one of my ~10 cross-button presses did literally nothing. Measuring the arms' pixel extents and clicking their centres (purple 408,264 / orange 376,292 / green 440,292 / cyan 408,324) instantly made them work.

2. **The red ring was a snake, not a lock.** The cross arms drive it 2 cells per press, but each arm is only *enabled* while the player stands on the matching pad of the isolated hub island (reached by recolouring the variable teleport node to cyan and using the magenta trapezoid, which is the universal teleport).

3. **Coupling + the double teleport.** Driving the snake so its hole engulfed the lever's red pivot let the RED BAR button contract the snake onto the pivot — after which the cross buttons dragged the whole 10-cell orange lever along the white track (right through the room, up the right corridor, left, then up the top corridor). Parked at rows 4–5 / cols 6–15 it exactly bridged the 10-cell gap between the isolated top-left pad and the goal platform. Since every magenta teleport also rotates the lever, I used **two** teleports (hub → variable node → yellow node) so the bridge was restored just as I arrived on the pad — then walked across it to the yellow goal at (23,3).
